task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 7, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style news update about Lenwick University's merger of two studio programs, addressing the practical consequences for current students and future applicants.

facts.text: Lenwick University announced Friday, Aug. 7, 2026, that its ceramics and furniture-design programs will share a new materials-design department.
The administrative merger takes effect in January 2027, while the first combined degree intake is planned for autumn 2027.
Current enrollment is 74 students in ceramics and 46 in furniture design, for a combined 120.
Current students may finish their existing degrees under the university's published completion plan.
Annual admission to the two programs has totaled 40 new students; the combined degree will admit 32.

The university will retain all nine full-time instructors but will not renew three part-time teaching contracts after the 2026–27 academic year; it has not disclosed how many individuals hold those contracts.
The new department will share drawing, materials-history and business-practice courses while retaining separate kiln and machine workshops.
Evening workshop access will end at 9 p.m. rather than 11 p.m. because the university is reducing staffed access hours.
Provost Iona Brill projects annual savings of $310,000 once the new curriculum is fully running.
That estimate includes reduced administration and part-time teaching but does not include a one-time workshop refit.
The university budgets $180,000 for a one-time workshop refit from an existing capital allocation; final expenditure is not yet known.
Third-year ceramics student Milo Fenn works afternoons at a grocery store and currently uses the workshop after 9 p.m.
Fenn said, "Finishing my degree is not just a promise about the name on the certificate. I need time at the kiln."
Brill said the department will seek student scheduling requests before publishing its January workshop timetable.
Local furniture maker Tavi Reed said shared materials training could be useful, but employers still need graduates who can operate specific equipment.
Reed said, "A broader course helps if there is still enough time to get good at a difficult tool."
The university has not released separate employment-outcome data for the existing programs.
Tuition for current students will not change as a result of the merger; autumn 2027 tuition has not been set.
The ceramics studio occupies a former railway goods office and includes a student-run shop open one afternoon a week.
The university's published plan retains the shop, which is operated as a supervised sales placement rather than a separate degree requirement.
